import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

def run(inputs: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    orders = inputs["orders"].copy()
    ref_customers = inputs["ref_customers"].copy()
    ref_skus = inputs["ref_skus"].copy()
    
    # Initialize result column with None (no failure)
    orders["reason_code"] = None
    
    # R1: customer_id not present in ref_customers
    valid_customers = set(ref_customers["customer_id"].dropna())
    mask_r1 = ~orders["customer_id"].isin(valid_customers)
    orders.loc[mask_r1 & (orders["reason_code"].isna()), "reason_code"] = "CUST_UNKNOWN"
    
    # R2: customer status <> 'ACTIVE'
    # Join with ref_customers to get status
    orders_with_status = orders.merge(
        ref_customers[["customer_id", "status"]], 
        on="customer_id", 
        how="left"
    )
    mask_r2 = (orders_with_status["status"] != "ACTIVE") & (orders_with_status["status"].notna())
    orders.loc[mask_r2 & (orders["reason_code"].isna()), "reason_code"] = "CUST_INACTIVE"
    
    # R3: sku not present in ref_skus
    valid_skus = set(ref_skus["sku"].dropna())
    mask_r3 = ~orders["sku"].isin(valid_skus)
    orders.loc[mask_r3 & (orders["reason_code"].isna()), "reason_code"] = "SKU_UNKNOWN"
    
    # R4: sku discontinued = 1
    # Join with ref_skus to get discontinued flag
    sku_discontinued_map = dict(zip(ref_skus["sku"], ref_skus["discontinued"]))
    orders["_discontinued"] = orders["sku"].map(sku_discontinued_map)
    mask_r4 = orders["_discontinued"] == 1
    orders.loc[mask_r4 & (orders["reason_code"].isna()), "reason_code"] = "SKU_DISC"
    
    # R5: allowed_countries non-empty AND ship_country not in list (trimmed)
    # Join with ref_skus to get allowed_countries
    sku_allowed_countries_map = dict(zip(ref_skus["sku"], ref_skus["allowed_countries"]))
    orders["_allowed_countries"] = orders["sku"].map(sku_allowed_countries_map)
    
    def is_country_blocked(row):
        allowed_countries_str = row["_allowed_countries"]
        ship_country = row["ship_country"]
        
        # Empty or NULL means all countries allowed
        if pd.isna(allowed_countries_str) or allowed_countries_str == "":
            return False
        
        # Parse comma-delimited list (trimmed)
        allowed = [c.strip() for c in str(allowed_countries_str).split(",")]
        allowed = [c for c in allowed if c]  # Remove empty strings after strip
        
        # If ship_country is null, treat as blocked if list is non-empty
        if pd.isna(ship_country):
            return len(allowed) > 0
        
        return str(ship_country) not in allowed
    
    mask_r5 = orders.apply(is_country_blocked, axis=1)
    orders.loc[mask_r5 & (orders["reason_code"].isna()), "reason_code"] = "CTRY_BLOCKED"
    
    # Split into clean and rejects
    orders_clean = orders[orders["reason_code"].isna()].copy()
    orders_rejects = orders[orders["reason_code"].notna()].copy()
    
    # Drop temporary columns
    orders_clean = orders_clean.drop(columns=["reason_code", "_discontinued", "_allowed_countries"])
    orders_rejects = orders_rejects.drop(columns=["_discontinued", "_allowed_countries"])
    
    # Ensure orders_rejects has reason_code column
    orders_rejects = orders_rejects[["order_id", "customer_id", "sku", "qty", "ship_country", "reason_code"]]
    
    return {
        "orders_clean": orders_clean,
        "orders_rejects": orders_rejects
    }
